Recap: A Tool Request and Its Execution

The database result becomes the observation for the next decision

Outline: Data Agents

01 · Understanding the Question

The Factory RequestA data agent uses tools to read records and make permitted changes

The read supplies evidence for a proposed change

What Does “Yield” Mean?Here, yield means good units divided by all produced units

The metric and selected records determine the answer

The Production RecordsP-17 has two runs with different output sizes

The second run produces one tenth as many units as the first

Tables and Machine IDsThe machine ID connects a machine to its production records

The query selects the two Runs rows for machine_id 1

Keys and Join RelationshipsTable relationships determine which records a query will combine

The join key connects records, while the primary key identifies a row

Yield by HandAdd the good counts and total counts, then divide

89 good units out of 110 total units gives 80.91% yield

Caveat: Averaging Run PercentagesGiving the two runs equal weight answers a different question

The larger run must contribute more to the combined yield

Join Multiplicity Changes TotalsA one-to-many join can duplicate one run before the sums are calculated

SUM after the join: (80 + 80 + 9) / (100 + 100 + 10)
Joining tags first gives the first run twice its intended weight

Evidence for a Query CheckKeep one numerical counterexample for each distinct failure

ConditionReturned yieldWhat went wrong
Correct machine, raw runs80.91%89 / 110
Equal weight per run85.00%Different metric
Run 1 duplicated by join80.48%Different row weights
SQL can run successfully while answering a different metric or weighting the wrong rows

Text-to-SQLThe model proposes a query using the question and table definitions

The SQL proposal still needs checking before execution

The SQL ProposalOne filter selects P-17, and two sums calculate its yield

SELECT SUM(good) AS good, SUM(total) AS total,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(good) / SUM(total), 2) AS yield_pct
FROM Runs
WHERE machine_id = 1;
goodtotalyield_pct
8911080.91
The database adds the counts for machine 1 before dividing

02 · Checking and Running a Read

Why Check the Proposal?A valid query can still select the wrong machine

Successful execution does not confirm that the request was understood

Checks Before a ReadMatch the request and use only permitted data

Meaning and access require checks beyond SQL syntax

Read and Write PermissionsPermission to inspect production does not grant permission to create repairs

The same user can have different permissions for reads and writes

Read-Only and Row ScopePreventing writes does not decide which machines a caller may read

A read-only query can still return a line B row unless row access is enforced

The Read ToolThe runtime sends the checked query to a read-only database operation

The tool returns database rows rather than an invented number

A Failed ReadUse the observed error to correct the query or stop

The answer needs a successful, permitted database read

No Rows and a Zero TotalAn unavailable ratio must not be reported as zero yield

Selected recordsSUM(good)SUM(total)Yield

No observed production is different from observed production with no good units

The Evidence for the AnswerReport the values and scope used in the calculation

The answer stays tied to the selected records

A Consistent ReadCalculate related counts from the same database snapshot

Before: 89 / 110 = 80.91%; after: 99 / 120 = 82.50%
One query returns 89/110 before the insert or 99/120 after it, rather than 89/120

A Low Yield Is Evidence for InspectionThe threshold triggers a proposed request, not a diagnosis

The requested change follows the user’s rule and observed result

03 · Making an Approved Change

Why Review the Change?“Fix P-17” does not identify what the system may change

The proposed effect must be concrete before approval

The Proposed Repair RequestThe preview identifies the target and values to be stored

The preview makes one database change reviewable

Design: Approval Before WritingThe application waits for a decision on this exact change

The approval gate is a design step, separate from the database demo

Approval and PermissionAn approved request must still fit the caller’s allowed scope

Approval does not expand database permissions

The Exact Approved ChangeApproval belongs to the reviewed target and payload, not to any later tool call

Reviewed requestActual requestDecision
req_42, machine 1, low yieldSame ID and same valuesExecute within permission
req_42, machine 1, low yieldmachine 3 insteadReject changed target
req_42, machine 1, low yieldreason changedReject changed payload
Changing the target or reason creates a different action from the one reviewed

The Write ToolCreate one repair and return its stored result

A successful receipt must correspond to a stored row

Caveat: Repeating a RequestA missing reply must not lead to a second repair request

The repeated request should refer to the same stored change

The Stored RequestVerify the row before reporting that the change succeeded

The completion message follows the database record

The Action RecordKeep the decision and outcome linked to the request

The record connects the intended change with its verified result

From Run View to an Audit RecordA path and message view helps locate a request; the database confirms its stored effect

An execution trace is useful evidence, but the stored row confirms the database change

Takeaway: Meaning, permission, and a verified result

1Check metric, join multiplicity, empty data and a consistent snapshot

3Approve the exact payload, preserve request identity and verify the stored effect
